images.filename: Swampy But Pretty Bog In Fiordland NZ.jpg
images.caption: A pretty bog on the Milford Track in Fiordland National Park, New Zealand. This boardwalk is part of a little educational side-trail shortly before arriving at the huts for the end of the first day of the (Freedom Walker's) track. Coordinates are approximate only (may be off as much as 50m).This photo was used around 2009 in a New Zealand Herald article about the Milford Track. Possibly only used in the online version though.

images.filename: No Deeper Waters On THIS Day Though.jpg
images.caption: A hiking path through a flood-prone area of the Milford Track in Fiordland National Park, New Zealand. When the water ponds in this area, the little signs are to show walkers where the path is. On some other stretches of the walk, walkers may even get transferred by helicopters over the flooded areas, because otherwise the whole oneway track movement, with the whole booking system, goes haywire. Gotta keep them moving!
images.alt: A hiking path through a flood-prone area of the Milford Track in Fiordland National Park, New Zealand. When the water ponds in this area, the little signs are to show walkers where the path is. images.caption:
Statue to Quintin Mackinnon near the Department of Conservation office in Te Anau. 
Inscription on base:
Quintin Mackinnon 1851-1892 Surveyor - Explorer - Guide
In 1888 Mackinnon and Ernest Mitchell were the first Europeans to travel overland from Lake Te Anau to Milford Sound

Their route became the world famous Milford Track
